bound: recordOperateLog is true by default and filter is registered on /erupt-api/*. No application-level JSON body limit found in reviewed code; multipart/file limits do not protect ordinary JSON body.
driver: request body byte volume, concurrent request count, servlet worker thread count
exploitability: Anonymous low-trust HTTP can trigger heap pressure before auth and may leave large bodies in thread-local storage on non-recorded paths. Exact OOM threshold requires default runtime probe.
retention: At least request-burst retention before business handling; on anonymous login, missing handler, auth failure, or handler without @EruptRecordOperate, the ThreadLocal body may remain attached to the worker thread until overwritten or thread exits
sink: HttpServletRequestFilter.EruptRequestWrapper reads the full request body with StreamUtils.copyToString and later duplicates it via body.getBytes(); RequestBodyTL.remove is only reached in OperationService for @EruptRecordOperate handlers
source: Any /erupt-api/* request with Content-Type exactly application/json and attacker-controlled body
static_status: No dynamic test run; static path and missing cleanup are concrete.
title: Default operation-log filter copies /erupt-api JSON body before auth and can retain it in ThreadLocal on non-recorded paths
